items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: I was raised in Indianapolis which was a wonderful musical environment, because Freddie Hubbard was there

ctx.x: That’s a great point. When you were growing up, did you have a musical family?

My mother and father, all my sisters and brothers were musicians. I was raised in Indianapolis which was a wonderful musical environment, because Freddie Hubbard was there, Wes Montgomery, J.J. Johnson, and just a lot of guys that were really very, very talented musicians that never became known. But we had a wonderful environment and the people there were very supportive of young people becoming musicians, in the high schools, marching band, they were very encouraging to us. So we were raised in an environment…
Kind of — what were the venues? Were they dances or just parties and that kind of thing?

items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So we were there living – Freddie Hubbard, myself, and two other guys in a room. We weren’t working at all. We practiced all the time.

ctx.x: How many nights a week were you working?
Sometimes we weren’t working at all, because we were new. So we were there living – Freddie Hubbard, myself, and two other guys in a room. We weren’t working at all. We practiced all the time.
This is the same room that you walked out of when you met Charlie Parker?
